compartments.text_span: This SIRS model assumes a constant total population n = s+i+r. Since we can determine the Recovered population from r = n − s − i, we only need unsteady population balances on the Susceptible and Infected classes.

the second term is the gain of Susceptibles due to loss of immunity (flux from Recovered to Susceptible class)
di/dt = βsi − νi, where the second term on the right-hand side represents the flux from the Infected to the Recovered class.

compartments.text_span: This model (Li et al., 1999) is similar to the previous example, except that recovery is possible, with recovery providing permanent immunity. Thus, there is now a Recovered population class, and there is no flux from the Recovered class to the Susceptible class.

compartments.text_span: Thus, there is now a Recovered population class, and there is no flux from the Recovered class to the Susceptible class. The only growth in the Susceptible class is from new births.
